title: High transposable element expression in sarcomas is associated with increased immune infiltrates and improved outcomes including after immunotherapy.
authors: Nacev, Benjamin A; Bradic, Martina; Woo, Hyung Jun; Richards, Allison L; Kelly, Ciara M; Dickson, Mark A; Gounder, Mrinal M; Keohan, Mary L; Chi, Ping; Movva, Sujana; Maki, Robert G; Slotkin, Emily K; Rosenbaum, Evan; Avutu, Viswatej; Chan, Jason E; Banks, Lauren B; Adamson, Travis; Singer, Samuel; Antonescu, Cristina R; Tap, William D; Donoghue, Mark Ta; D'Angelo, Sandra P
one_liner_zh: 该文研究肉瘤中转座子表达与免疫浸润及免疫治疗结局的关联，虽涉及转录因子IKZF1但仅作表达相关性分析，无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题核心无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Response to immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) in sarcomas is overall low and heterogeneous. Understanding determinants of ICI outcomes may improve efficacy and patient selection. Thus, we investigated whether the expression of transposable elements (TEs), which are epigenetically silenced and can stimulate antitumor immunity, influence ICI outcomes and immune infiltrates in common sarcoma subtypes. METHODS: We used transcriptomic data to assign immune enhanced versus immune depleted status to 67 pretreatment and on-treatment biopsies of sarcomas from patients treated on ICI trials, along with additional cohorts from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and an independent ICI trial (SARC028). A machine learning technique (lasso-penalized logistic regression) controlled for sarcoma subtype was used to determine if TE and epigenetic regulatory gene expression predict immune infiltrates. Correlations between top features in these models and sarcoma immune infiltrates, immune pathway expression, and clinical outcomes were explored. RESULTS: Expression of TEs and epigenetic regulators significantly predicted immune enhanced status. TE subfamilies and Ikaros family zinc finger 1 (IKZF1), a chromatin-modulating transcription factor, were significantly contributory. TE and IKZF1 expression positively correlated with tumor immune infiltrates, inflammatory pathways, and improved clinical outcomes, and increased in tumors that gained immune infiltrates during ICI treatment. TE and IKZF1 expression similarly correlated with overall survival and immune features in a TCGA cohort. In an additional cohort of patients with sarcoma treated with ICI, IKZF1 expression correlated with progression-free survival and inflammatory features. CONCLUSIONS: TE and IKZF1 expression warrant further translational investigation as potential biomarkers of tumor immune infiltrates and outcomes following ICI treatment, and as therapeutic targets in sarcomas.
abstract_zh: 背景：肉瘤对免疫检查点抑制（ICI）治疗的反应总体较低且具有异质性。了解ICI疗效的决定因素可能提高治疗效果并改善患者选择。因此，我们研究了转座元件（TEs）的表达（这些元件在表观遗传上被沉默，且可刺激抗肿瘤免疫）是否影响常见肉瘤亚型中的ICI疗效和免疫浸润。方法：我们使用转录组数据，将来自ICI试验患者的67份治疗前和治疗中肉瘤活检样本，以及来自癌症基因组图谱（TCGA）和独立ICI试验（SARC028）的额外队列，分配为免疫增强或免疫耗竭状态。采用机器学习技术（lasso惩罚逻辑回归）控制肉瘤亚型，以确定TE和表观遗传调控基因表达是否能预测免疫浸润。探讨了这些模型中顶级特征与肉瘤免疫浸润、免疫通路表达及临床结局之间的相关性。结果：TE和表观遗传调控因子的表达显著预测了免疫增强状态。TE亚家族和Ikaros家族锌指蛋白1（IKZF1）（一种染色质调节转录因子）具有显著贡献。TE和IKZF1表达与肿瘤免疫浸润、炎症通路及改善的临床结局呈正相关，并在ICI治疗期间获得免疫浸润的肿瘤中表达增加。在TCGA队列中，TE和IKZF1表达与总生存期和免疫特征同样相关。在另一个接受ICI治疗的肉瘤患者队列中，IKZF1表达与无进展生存期和炎症特征相关。结论：TE和IKZF1表达值得进一步转化研究，作为ICI治疗后肿瘤免疫浸润和结局的潜在生物标志物，以及肉瘤中的治疗靶点。
